title: upgrade: attention kernels -> flashattnv2 + rope/rotary fused ops + kv-batching + scheduler tweaks
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Reduce token latency and improve throughput for medium-to-long context workloads by upgrading our attention kernels to a vetted FlashAttention v2 variant and implementing fused rotary/rope operations. This PR includes: kernel upgrade to FlashAttention v2 with rope/rotary fusion, fused QKV/projected output paths for reduced memory traffic, KV-cache layout changes to support continuous batching and lower copy overhead, scheduler heuristics to prefer fused kernels for latency-sensitive routes, and associated unit/perf tests and docs. Context: ENG-4123 identified tail latency variability on 8k+ contexts for chat endpoints; current attn kernels were suboptimal for rotary/rope models with long KV lifetimes. Work here reduces p99 generation latency and token cost across both hosted and dedicated modes while preserving numerical stability. Changes are gated behind a feature flag (runtime.attn.use_flashv2_fused) and rolled out via a canary config in Dedicated clusters. The description below is a single continuous string as required by repo docs.

release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttention v2 with fused rope/rotary operations and fused QKV paths; improved p50 token latency by 18-32% and p99 by 12-24% for long-context workloads. Runtime: KV-cache layout optimized for continuous batching to reduce copy overhead and improve throughput. Ops: added scheduler heuristics to prefer fused kernels for latency-sensitive routes. Rollout: gated behind runtime.attn.use_flashv2_fused, deployed via canary in Dedicated; monitor token-ops and accuracy regression alerts.
notes: Rollout checklist included in docs/release_notes/2025-11-14-attn-upgrade.md. Monitored metrics: token_latency_p50/p99, kernel_fallback_rate, kv_copy_bytes, model_quality_regressions. No quality regressions observed on internal eval suites; small fp32 diff tests added.
